texts.facts: The brief facts of the case are that on 29.09.2022 at about 10:00/10:30 a.m. an Ecco Van no. DL-3CCM-8484 (hereinafter refereed to as the offending vehicle) came driven at a high speed, in a rash and negligent manner and hit the kiosk of one Bablu (neighbour of claimant). When claimant tried to turn of its DVR, instead of halting the offending vehicle, its driver drove away the offending vehicle. The offending vehicle continued to drive at a very high speed towards MB Road with sudden jerks and also hit against a Passion Pro motorcycle bearing no.DLSEK0789 on which two persons were riding. 3. On complaint of the injured an FIR no. 0393/2022 was registered u/s 279/337 of IPC against respondent no.1. Upon investigation chargesheet was filed u/s 279/304-A/337/338 IPC before concerned criminal court and DAR was filed before this Tribunal. Respondent no.1 is the driver, respondent no.2 is the owner (since deceased) of the offending vehicle and respondent no.3 is the insurance company with which such offending vehicle was insured. 5. Despite opportunity none of the respondents file any written statement. There is no statutory defence raised by any of the respondents and thus, there is no technical requirement of even framing of issues in as much as the fact of accident occurring due to rash and negligent driving has not been disputed.
texts.arguments: If an allegation is denied, the respondent must state his reasons for the denial and if necessary, put forward his own version of events. As regards the quantum of compensation and the respondent who is liable to pay the same, this court is governed by the law laid down by Hon'le Supreme Court in Raj Kumar Vs. Ajay Kumar & Anr. (2011) 1 Supreme Court cases 343, Sarla Verma & Ors. v. Delhi Transport Corporation & Ors. (2003) 6SCC 121 and National Insurance Company Limited v. Pranay Sethi & Ors.(2017) 16 SCC 680. The gist of the law is that the object of awarding damages is to make good the loss suffered as MACT No: 123/23 Govind Gupta vs Vikash @ Vikcy & ors. The court or the Tribunal shall have to assess the damages objectively and exclude from consideration any speculation or fancy, though some conjecture with reference to the nature of disability and its consequences, is inevitable. A person is not only to be compensated for the physical injury, but also for the loss which he suffered as a result of such injury. 11.
